answer: Surge-priced entry: every new agent must burn a join fee that rises with how many accounts joined in the last day, so a quiet zephyr of sign-ups stays cheap while a flood quickly gets expensive. An attacker spawning a thousand fakes pays a steeper fee for each one, and the cost curve bends upward at the vertex of the spike. Honest newcomers who arrive alone pay little; a Sybil burst only hears its own echo in an ever-larger bill.
